Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

TEXT_E:
This 2001 manifesto sets out a second-term program focused on economic stability, improved public services, welfare modernization, safer communities, and an active international role.

Core pledges for the next five years:
- Economy: Maintain low inflation, keep mortgages as low as possible, and ensure sound public finances.
- Schools: Recruit 10,000 additional teachers and raise standards in secondary education.
- Health: Recruit 20,000 more nurses and 10,000 more doctors, with continued reform of the National Health Service and faster treatment free at the point of use.
- Crime: Add 6,000 police recruits to reach the highest police numbers to date.
- Families: Retain the winter fuel payment for pensioners and raise the minimum wage to £4.20.

Longer-term goals for 2010:
- Sustained economic stability and rising living standards.
- Expanded higher education, underpinned by stronger secondary school performance.
- A healthier nation with faster, free treatment.
- Full employment across all regions.
- Greater opportunity for children and improved security for pensioners.
- A modernized criminal justice system.
- Strong, accountable local government.
- Leadership in a reformed, enlarged European framework.
- Action on global poverty and climate change.

Planned actions:
- Economy and skills: Preserve stability; invest in skills, infrastructure, and technology; prioritize basic skills for adults; and pursue higher productivity to boost living standards nationwide.
- Public services: Build on primary school progress to transform secondary schools; invest in and empower NHS staff to modernize care; broaden access to culture and sport.
- Welfare: Restructure benefits to emphasize support into work; enhance support for children and families through the tax and benefits system; and improve cash and services for pensioners.
- Communities and justice: Reform the criminal justice system to improve detection, punishment, and rehabilitation; increase police capacity; tackle drugs and the causes of crime; and strengthen local community responsibility alongside resources.
- International and Europe: Engage fully in Europe, support enlargement and institutional reform, and commit to a public vote on any proposal to join the euro; advance policies on aid, development, debt relief, and environmental protection.

Reported results since 1997 include lower inflation and unemployment, approximately one million more people in work, reductions in NHS waiting lists and times alongside rising nurse and doctor numbers, the best recorded primary school results, a 10% fall in crime (British Crime Survey), and lower typical mortgage costs. The manifesto frames these as foundations for further reform and investment.

TEXT_D:
Summary of proposals (2001)

Health
- Cut waiting times by recruiting 27,500 nurses, 4,600 doctors, 10,250 allied health professionals; add 10,000 hospital beds.
- Improve retention with average £1,000 pay rises for lowest-paid NHS staff; commission on NHS pay and conditions.
- Free personal care for elderly/long-term patients; restore free dental and eye checks; double investment in scanners; £500m to guarantee NHS dentistry access.
- Create a Pharmaceutical Agency to end “postcode lottery,” use NHS purchasing power, and move toward scrapping prescription charges.
- Patient Care Guarantees; stronger local accountability; independent advocacy (incl. Children’s Rights Commissioner); no-fault compensation; end mixed wards; ban age discrimination in care.

Education, skills and work
- Primary classes averaged at 25; recruit 5,000 extra secondary teachers; 40,000 classroom assistants (25,000 in Key Stage 1); two paid prep hours weekly for primary teachers; paid training salary for trainees; reduce bureaucracy and testing at age 7.
- Abolish university tuition fees; restore grants for poorer students; raise loan repayment threshold; oppose top-up fees; improve HE staff pay.
- Adult entitlement to funded tuition (to Level 2; to Level 3 for 16–24s); merge skills funders into a Learning Council; SME training incentives; paid study leave for 16–24s; replace New Deal with a Flexible Guarantee via a combined Benefits and Jobs Agency.

Law, order and justice
- 6,000 additional police officers; 2,000 part-time retained community officers; Community Safety Force for low-level disorder.
- Independent police complaints system; community-focused partnerships; cooperation with Europol.
- Shift from costly prison expansion to effective alternatives; full working day, skills and rehabilitation in prisons; reduce reoffending.
- Stronger victims’ rights (impact statements, information); tackle hate crimes; retain jury trial; end most mandatory sentencing; expand restorative and youth justice reforms.

Transport
- Free off-peak local bus travel for pensioners and disabled people; aim half-price fares for under-19s in education.
- Abolish Vehicle Excise Duty for the cleanest vehicles; higher VED for most polluting; no real-terms rise in fuel duty next Parliament.
- Enable local funding tools (bonds, congestion charging, parking levies); create a Sustainable Transport Authority; stronger public control of rail investment and safety; restructure rail infrastructure into a not-for-profit public-interest model; rural transport fund; priority to road maintenance and safety; not-for-profit air traffic control; tighter night flight limits.

Pensions, wages and benefits
- Increase basic state pension (£5/week single; more for over-75s/80s; proportional rises for couples); scrap savings penalty; establish an Independent Pensions Authority; relax annuity rules; develop personal second pensions and extend basic entitlement over time.
- Annual review of the minimum wage; single full rate from age 16.
- Extra £200 for children in families on long-term income support; replace the Child Support Agency with family courts.
- Improve support for disabled people (incl. winter fuel payments for the severely disabled); simplify housing benefit; fairer utility tariffs; better cold weather payments; reduce tax on the lowest paid over time.

Culture, media and sport
- Embed arts in schools; restore free instrumental tuition funding; lower VAT on renovation (and apply low rate to new build); universal free internet access in libraries.
- Create OFCOM; redefine public service broadcasting; reform BBC governance; tighter cross-media ownership; community sports plans.

Business, consumers and environment
- Scrap unnecessary regulations; small business rates allowance; stronger competition law; improved consumer and bank protections; Post Office universal service.
- Replace the Climate Change Levy with a carbon tax; emissions trading; at least 10% renewable energy by 2010 rising annually; phase out nuclear as stations retire; expand research funding; ethical corporate reporting.

Political and civil rights
- Referendum on AV+ for Westminster; STV for local/European elections; voting and candidacy from 16; elected Senate to replace the Lords; stronger parliamentary scrutiny; local income tax.
- Stronger Freedom of Information; Equality Act and Equality Commission; civil partnership registration; judicial oversight of surveillance; no ID cards.
- Fairer, faster asylum system; end vouchers; improve support and local compensation.

Communities, rural and housing
- National doorstep recycling (60% in 10 years); flood defence task force; GM crop moratorium until 2004; marine protected areas.
- One-stop regeneration grants; brownfield-first with planning and VAT reform; protect green spaces; require planning for mobile masts.
- Reform CAP/CFP toward sustainability and local co-management; support tenant and organic farming; create a Ministry for Rural Affairs; protect village services; measures on affordability, empty homes, and leasehold rights; option for site value rating.

Europe, defence and international
- EU constitutional settlement clarifying powers; subsidiarity and transparency; accountable Commission/Council; enlargement; single Parliament seat in Brussels.
- Maintain defence spending; flexible, deployable forces; retain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing disarmament; oppose national missile defence; moratorium on depleted uranium.
- End subsidies for arms exports; strengthen UN (incl. rapid reaction/disaster capacity, ICC); fairer WTO rules with environmental integration; aid to 0.7% GNI, untied and focused on gender, health (HIV/AIDS), and education; stronger climate commitments (e.g., CO2 −20% by 2010).

Economy and tax
- Enhance Bank of England independence (non-renewable MPC terms, transparent appointments).
- Enable euro entry via referendum at a competitive rate.
- Allow devolved/regional/local borrowing for investment.
- Fund priorities through 1p on income tax for education; 50% top rate above £100k for pensions and NHS; CGT simplification; Citizen’s Tax Contract; annual independent fiscal assessment; green tax reform matched by cuts elsewhere; reduce tax burden on lowest incomes over time.
